statements.statement: WriterHistoryCache and ReaderProxy change tracking remain coherent when a CacheChange is removed from history.
StatefulWriter HEARTBEAT firstSN/lastSN is derived from the current WriterHistoryCache sequence-number bounds.
ACKNACK-requested changes are retransmitted from WriterHistoryCache after nackResponseDelay processing.
add_change assigns monotonically increasing sequence numbers and inserts changes into the writer HistoryCache.
KEEP_LAST cache depth evicts oldest changes when full.
matched_reader_add enables subsequent data sends to a matched reader locator.
TRANSIENT_LOCAL matched readers receive replay-marked cached changes.

A reliable TRANSIENT_LOCAL writer piggybacks a non-final HEARTBEAT spanning its cache on the newest change it replays to a newly matched reader, so the reader acknowledges or requests repairs without waiting for the periodic HEARTBEAT.

A matched reader whose cumulative acknowledgement goes backwards has matched the writer again after a lease expiry (§8.5.3.2) and receives what matched_reader_add gives a new reader: TRANSIENT_LOCAL replay, or GAP for earlier changes when VOLATILE.
tick() emits periodic HEARTBEAT messages according to heartbeatPeriod.
on_acknack processes cumulative acknowledgment state and ignores duplicate count values.

An ACKNACK requesting nothing from a reader that has acknowledged nothing yet, while the writer has written more, is answered with a HEARTBEAT directed at that reader; a plain ACK from a reader that has acknowledged before is not answered, so HEARTBEATs never pair with ACKNACKs into a per-round-trip exchange while the writer streams.
on_nack_frag arms deferred retransmit and tick() sends requested data after nackResponseDelay.
requested_changes_set marks NACKed changes REQUESTED, next_requested_change returns the lowest REQUESTED change, and acked_changes_set clears acknowledged requests.
next_unsent_change returns the lowest UNSENT change relevant to the reader, and unacked_changes is non-empty until the newest relevant change is acknowledged.

A reliable StatefulWriter piggybacks a non-final HEARTBEAT on the DATA of every depth/2-th write, in the same RTPS message when the DATA can end on a 4-octet boundary within the datagram limit (a copied DATA is padded and the padding recorded in the encapsulation options), and in a datagram of its own otherwise; a periodic HEARTBEAT restarts the count.

A VOLATILE StatefulWriter removes a change from its history once every matched reader has acknowledged it (RELIABLE) or been sent it (BEST_EFFORT), or at once when no reader is matched, returning its payload to the pool; a TRANSIENT_LOCAL writer keeps acknowledged changes for late-joining readers; a NACK for a removed change is answered with GAP.

A service reply writer (TRANSIENT_LOCAL) removes a reply once every matched reader sharing the GUID prefix of the request writer named in its related sample identity has acknowledged it, independent of other readers; a reply whose requester has not matched yet stays and is delivered when that reader matches; a reply whose requester's last matched reader unmatches is removed.

A reliable StatefulWriter answers a NACK_FRAG, once nackResponseDelay has passed, by resending exactly the named fragments of the change followed by a HEARTBEAT; a NACK_FRAG whose count is not above the last processed from that reader is ignored; one for a change no longer held is answered with GAP.
A StatefulWriter sends to a matched reader at its unicastLocatorList; the ReaderProxy refers to the owning record's entry and sends to its current value, never to an emptied entry.

Matched-endpoint proxies come from a fixed pool shared by a participant's endpoints. An endpoint below its floor always binds a proxy; at or above it, an endpoint binds only a proxy no floor is promised; no endpoint exceeds its cap; free >= reserved holds after every bind and release.
An endpoint's bound proxies are iterated in the order they matched and are shared with no other endpoint; a released proxy is free for any endpoint.
